summary: Curry County, OR: a 1930 R-1 ground cabin on Long Ridge, demolished in 1962 after the Columbus Day storm; duties moved to Quail Prairie in 1963.

facts.design: 14 by 14 foot R-1 style ground cabin
facts.status_note: Demolished after the October 1962 Columbus Day storm; firelookout.com says destroyed in that storm

events.note: N.B. Moore named as a fire watcher posted at Long Ridge; predates the 1930 cabin
14 by 14 foot R-1 style ground cabin built on Long Ridge
Four miles of road completed up Long Ridge to the lookout house, July 1930
Forest plan: station principally necessary for lightning; probably overlooks man-caused fires to the southwest
Station staffed 94 days; reported to Gold Beach station by telephone
Activated March 21, 1942; Roseburg Filter Center named on the Forest Lookouts page
Destroyed in the Columbus Day storm; a newspaper item dated October 23, 1962 says demolished
Lookout duties moved to the Quail Prairie Mountain tower, constructed in 1963

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says '1930: 2 cabins'. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1930 Siskiyou Bulletin notice that the district drew two new cabins, one for Long Ridge and one for Packsaddle. The story counts one cabin at Long Ridge, as the Forest inventory does.
The Forest Lookouts page names a fireman stationed at Long Ridge in 1916. The Forest inventory calls the 1930 cabin the first lookout for the area. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Demolition is in the Forest inventory and the Forest Lookouts newspaper item; firelookout.com gives only Columbus Day 1962, so no exact day is recorded. The 1963 transfer year is inferred from Quail Prairie's construction date; the Forest Lookouts page does not date the transfer, so treat the 1963 'replaced' event as approximate. The FFLA entry for Quail Prairie carries an asterisk that the list does not explain; the story reports 'standing' without the asterisk. A Facebook history post surfaced in search but was not read or cited.
